topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, course structure, and key learning outcomes regarding cancer causation and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Genetic Predisposition, Endogenous Mutagenesis, and Environmental Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the conceptual framework of cancer development, weighing the contributions of intrinsic genetic factors, bad luck, and environmental exposures through epidemiological evidence.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens and Oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how infectious agents, including bacteria, parasites, and viruses, contribute to malignancy, featuring Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Carcinogenesis: Initiation, Promotion, and Host Factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how dietary, chemical, and physical carcinogens cause malignancy through metabolic activation, DNA adduct formation, chronic inflammation, tumor promotion, and developmental timing.

topics.label: Methodologies for Assessing Carcinogenicity and Mutagenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the experimental and analytical methods—including whole-genome mutational signatures, epidemiological biobanks, in vivo toxicological models, and the in vitro Ames test—used to identify carcinogens.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with closing remarks on evaluating carcinogenic risk versus practical benefit in everyday exposures.
